body:
maria: heads up — audit-bot flagged a weird access pattern to billing_aggregates this morning. looks like a non-admin role briefly read aggregated cost/usage fields :eyes:
jon: saw the alert. which role? any repro steps from the logs?
audit-bot: detected: 2026-03-18T08:12:03Z read on table billing_aggregates by service_account:svc-ingest-qa-role (role_id: ingestion_viewer_v2)
maria: exact. svc-ingest-qa-role is supposed to only have metric-read for raw telemetry, not cost or per-customer usage.
rachel: is this the RBAC migration we ran last week? there were changes to how we map old roles -> new perms. could be a mapping gap.
jon: yep, last-week migration script included `role_map_v2` push. quick grep shows `ingestion_viewer_v2` inherits `usage_read` in the new mapping — looks accidental. snippet:
```
# role_map_v2 excerpt
ingestion_viewer_v2: [telemetry_read, metric_agg_read, usage_read]
```
shouldn't have `usage_read` though.
maria: whew. so the mapping accidentally granted `usage_read` which lifts visibility into cost buckets and quota counters. this explains the audit event.
sam: impact triage: which customers' data was accessible? audit-bot has a pre-aggregate dump id — can we narrow by query_id?
audit-bot: query_id=aq-20260318-081203, affected_range=2026-03-01..2026-03-17, returned fields: {customer_id, total_tokens, cost_estimate_usd} — access was via internal analytics API using service token.
rachel: blocker for P0: if any customer-identifying fields plus cost were exposed, we need to notify legal + cs.
jon: immediate remediation: rollback role_map_v2 change for ingestion_viewer_v2 and revoke active tokens for svc-ingest-qa-role. I'll open a rollback PR and a short-lived emergency policy until we do a safer patch.
maria: make sure KMS key usage audit is included — tokens are signed by tok-service using key `kms/prod/tokens`. check key rotation logs too.
jon: calling it out — running `gcloud kms keys versions list` + tok-service logs. also will revoke the single service account key: `gcloud iam service-accounts keys delete <key>`
sam: ops: prepare canary patch to remove `usage_read` inheritance and add an allowlist check for `billing_aggregates` access at the API layer. we should also add an audit rule: deny responses that include cost_estimate_usd unless caller has `billing_admin` role.
jon: created PR #4521 (emergency/rbac-rollback-ingest), and a hotfix branch with middleware check. linking in ticket: SEC-7832.
maria: good. timeline?
jon: revoking keys now (started 08:50). PR tested on staging, deploying middleware gate to canary (10% traffic) next 15m. will rotate service token after cut.
rachel: i'll draft the customer notification template in #legal and loop in CS. keep wording "limited internal visibility" until we confirm scope.
sam: post-mortem asks: add unit tests for role mapping, add CI check that role_map diffs are reviewed by sec, and ensure `usage_read` scoping is explicit (not transitive).
maria: add audit log retention spike: increase detailed logs for billing_aggregates queries to 90 days for now and export to secure bucket (kms encrypted). ticket SEC-7833.
deploy-bot: deploy stage=canary service=analytics-gateway user=jon status=STARTED
deploy-bot: deploy stage=canary service=analytics-gateway user=jon status=SUCCESS duration=2m12s
jon: canary looks clean. middleware blocked 7 calls that would've returned cost fields. rolling to 50% now.
maria: great. follow-ups: (1) patch role_map_v2 to remove usage_read inheritance and make mapping explicit; (2) implement API-level allowlist for sensitive fields; (3) schedule KMS key audit and rotate tok-service key; (4) add SEC postmortem and CS/legal notification.
rachel: noted. i'll schedule a short cross-team sync at 11:30 to confirm messaging and next steps.
maria: thanks everyone. filing short incident note under SEC-2026-03-18 and assigning owners.
jon: PR merged to main at 09:42, applying migration to roll back mapping. will post final status once service tokens rotated.
audit-bot: incident SEC-2026-03-18 created, severity=medium, owners=[maria, jon, rachel, sam]
